title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Claims and Remittance Posting
content:
Reimbursement and billing manual section: payer claims and remittance posting for the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

## 1. Claims

1.1 Every refill shipped on a payer tier is billed to the payer named by the program's coverage record by one original claim per shipment, with the ship date as the date of service; the CGM Self-Pay Program files no claims.

1.2 An original claim must be transmitted no later than the tier's timely-filing limit (calendar days) after the date of service of the shipment it bills, counted in calendar days from that ship date with the last day allowed; a shipment whose filing limit has passed is billed to neither the payer nor the customer and is written off by Larkfield.

1.3 A corrected claim replaces an original claim when the units, item or dates billed were wrong or some of the units were returned, and a void claim withdraws an original claim when all of its units were returned; both reference the same shipment as the original.

## 2. Remittances and patient responsibility

2.1 When a remittance posts, the patient responsibility added to the customer's balance is the allowed amount less the amount the payer paid, which the remittance itemizes as deductible, coinsurance and copay.

2.2 Larkfield never posts more than that and never bills the customer the difference between its billed charge and the allowed amount on a payer tier.

2.3 On tiers where crossover to secondary coverage is automatic and the customer has an in-effect secondary coverage record, the patient responsibility is crossed over to the secondary payer, and the secondary payer's payment is posted as a balance adjustment with reason secondary payer payment against that remittance before any amount is statemented; on other tiers a secondary coverage is billed by Larkfield's billing team only after the primary remittance posts.

2.4 On the CGM Medicaid Program a customer is never billed for a Medicaid-covered item beyond the patient responsibility the Medicaid remittance shows.

## 3. Worked figures (hypothetical)

- **Patient responsibility.** A remittance shows an allowed amount of 250.00 USD and a payer payment of 200.00 USD: the patient responsibility posted is 250.00 USD less 200.00 USD, that is 50.00 USD, whatever Larkfield's billed charge was.
- **Filing limit.** Suppose the limit were 90 days and the ship date 1 January of a non-leap year. A claim transmitted on 1 April, the ninetieth calendar day after the ship date, is timely; one transmitted on 2 April is late, and the shipment is written off.

| Claim action | Used when |
|---|---|
| Original claim | Once per refill shipment on a payer tier |
| Corrected claim | Units, item or dates billed were wrong, or some units were returned |
| Void claim | All of the claim's units were returned |
